trickyParts: Harness: /legion/scratch/harness-527/setup.sh (idempotent) and env.sh (source only around harness commands; per-LEGION_ROLE ports: implementer 18777/19021-19024, tester 28777/29021-29024, reviewer 38777/39021-39024; DB_URL/DB_BASE_URL dispatch_527_<role>[_base] on the pod's one Postgres at 127.0.0.1:55432, which is left running). PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH is not set: Chromium is in XDG_CACHE_HOME's shared registry (tools.md).
Some specs import packages/contracts/dist: run `bun run build` in packages/contracts once (done in the workspace and in /legion/scratch/infra-527-base).
Pass test files before --project (`bun run e2e -- <files> --project=chromium`); --project is variadic and swallows file names.
A `timeout` around `bun run e2e` leaves the four fake listeners running on the lane's ports; stop them by exact PID before the next run.
A Conversation comment turn is collapsed to a one-line MarkdownPreview until 'Expand thread' is clicked (a full-screen Thread dialog on iphone); the A1 rows expand first.

Chromium paints a disabled native checkbox pale grey; the box is drawn with appearance:none so a tick reads in light mode. Firefox draws no pseudo-elements on an input, so the tick is a background image.
deviations: Plan D4 said no accent-color and the native box's colours; the native disabled box's tick was hard to see in light mode (screenshot), so the box is drawn with appearance:none, filled in the link blue with a contrasting tick. It stays a native disabled checkbox.

Added the dark-mode Markdown link colour fix (adjacent defect in the same .dispatch-markdown CSS block: links stayed sky-700 on dark cards since #919) with its own browser row, per the repository's rule that a clear defect in code a tree touches is fixed in that tree's pull request. The architect was told.
Plan's harness note set PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH; skill://legion-worker/references/tools.md says not to, so env.sh leaves it unset.

Round 2: the look-different check compares decoded pixels with a 10% threshold of strong (>=128 per channel) differences, not raw bytes: two identically drawn boxes still differed in a few antialiased edge pixels, so a byte compare passed without the forced-colors rules.
Round 2: the reviewer's fast-follow items (shared assertions helper, shared Thread-dialog scope helper, pointer-events comment) were done in this round rather than deferred.
openQuestions: The one-line preview (collapsed Conversation turn) still shows no tick state, per plan D5; sent to the INFRA-138 architect in round one, no answer received.
